name: Wan 2.2 Bernini-R — video editing with a reference image
title: Copy an outfit onto a video
summary: Give it a clip of a person and a photo of clothes — worn by someone or on a hanger — and the person in the clip comes back wearing them, with the same face, moves and scene. Takes several minutes; keep clips short.
description:
Put the clothes from a photo onto the person in a short video. Upload a clip, a reference photo of an outfit and an instruction — the Bernini-R model (Wan 2.2) regenerates the clip so the person wears that outfit, keeping their face, the scene, the motion and the timing. A photo of the clothes worn by someone works better than clothes laid flat. The original audio is carried through.

Write the instruction as the swap plus what must stay, like the default: "Replace the person's clothing with the outfit from the reference image. Keep the face, hair, background, lighting, camera and all motion unchanged." Describing the new outfit and the result helps. This card is for outfit and look swaps, not for copying the general style of a picture: in one test, asking it to match the look of a poster changed only the sky.

• **Edit type**: keep "Video Editing with Reference". "Ads / Content Insertion" here only changes the model's first instruction line: Bernini's real ad-insertion task takes a second video, which this card has no slot for.
• **Fast mode** (Turbo LoRA) is on by default — ~6 steps. Turn it off for slower, higher-quality 40-step runs.
• Only the first few seconds are processed (set the clip length) — keep clips short, video editing is heavy.

For editing by text alone (no reference image), use the plain video-editing version instead.
